title: Identifiability through government ID and personal data
description: The parent user shares government ID, name, and email during registration, which can be used to identify them across systems or databases. This creates a risk of re-identification even if other data is anonymized.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: The registration data (email, password, name, government ID, six-digit code) is transmitted in transit and could be intercepted by attackers, potentially allowing credential theft or identity usurpation.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive registration data
description: The authentication service receives and stores highly sensitive personal data including government ID and authentication codes. Improper access controls or data retention policies could lead to unauthorized disclosure.

title: Linkability of registration data across systems
description: The registration data contains identifiers (email, name, government ID) that could be used to link this user's data across different systems or time periods, potentially creating a comprehensive profile.

title: Lack of non-repudiation for registration submission
description: The parent user may not be able to prove they did not submit the registration data, or the system may not be able to prove the user's identity at the time of registration, creating potential disputes.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Parent Account Data
description: The MongoDB users collection stores sensitive parent account information that could be accessed by unauthorized parties through database breaches, insider threats, or inadequate access controls.

title: Identification of Account Holders via Stored Parent Account Data
description: The stored parent account data contains personally identifiable information that could be used to identify individual account holders, potentially leading to privacy violations.

title: Data Integrity Compromise of Stored Parent Account Data
description: The stored parent account data could be tampered with or corrupted during storage, leading to inaccurate authentication records and potential security vulnerabilities.

title: Inappropriate Data Sharing by Authentication Service
description: The Authentication Service may share parent account data with the MongoDB collection without proper justification or minimization, exposing unnecessary personal information.

title: Identifiability of User Data in Transit
description: User data transmitted in JWT format may contain personally identifiable information that could be extracted or linked to the parent user during transmission.

title: Linkability of User Data Across Systems
description: The JWT and user data could be used to link the parent user's identity across different systems or services, potentially enabling correlation of activities.

title: Usurpation of User Identity by Parent User
description: The parent user may misuse the received JWT and user data to impersonate the authenticated user or access unauthorized resources.

title: Disclosure of User Data at Source
description: The Authentication Service may share user data with the parent user without adequate access controls or data minimization, leading to unnecessary exposure.

title: Linkability of child's identity through parent credentials
description: The child user sharing parent email and password at the source could link their identity to other data systems or profiles, potentially revealing associations between the child and parent accounts.

title: Identification of child through parent authentication data
description: The parent email and password shared by the child could directly identify the child's account and potentially reveal the child's identity to unauthorized parties.

title: Disclosure of credentials in transit
description: Parent email and password data in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties through network eavesdropping or man-in-the-middle attacks.

title: Insecure storage of authentication credentials
description: The authentication service may store parent email and password data without adequate encryption or access controls, leading to potential unauthorized access.

title: Usurpation of child's authentication
description: The child user could be impersonated by an unauthorized party who obtains the parent email and password, leading to unauthorized access to child's account.

title: Usurpation of authentication service
description: The authentication service could be impersonated by an attacker, causing the child to submit credentials to a fraudulent service.

title: Identification via intercepted JWT and child profiles
description: JWT tokens and child profiles transmitted in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, enabling identification of the child user through sensitive personal data contained in the tokens and profiles

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile data
description: The Authentication Service may share child profile data with the Child User without proper authorization, consent, or appropriate access controls in place

title: Unauthorized use of received authentication and profile data
description: The Child User may use the received JWT and profile data for unauthorized purposes beyond the intended scope, such as impersonation or accessing unauthorized services

title: Identification of child through government ID sharing
description: Parent shares child's government ID during profile creation, which directly identifies the child and creates a permanent identifier that can be used to uniquely identify them across systems.

title: Linkability of child profile through government ID
description: Government ID serves as a unique identifier that could link this child profile to other databases, records, or systems, potentially enabling cross-referencing and profiling of the child.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's government ID
description: The child profile management process may store or transmit the government ID without adequate access controls, potentially exposing it to unauthorized parties.

title: Identity usurpation through child's government ID
description: The government ID could be stolen or misused by malicious actors to impersonate the child in other systems, leading to identity theft or fraudulent activities.

title: Regulatory non-compliance in government ID handling
description: Storing and processing government ID may violate GDPR or other data protection regulations regarding sensitive personal data, particularly concerning children's data protection requirements.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Child Profile Data
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB collection could be accessed by unauthorized parties through database breaches, insider threats, or inadequate access controls, leading to privacy violations of children and their guardians.

title: Data Integrity Compromise
description: Child profile data could be tampered with, corrupted, or altered during storage or update operations, potentially leading to incorrect information being used for decisions affecting the child.

title: Data Unavailability
description: Child profile data could become unavailable due to MongoDB service outages, data corruption, or storage failures, preventing authorized access when needed.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Storing children's personal data may violate GDPR and other child protection regulations if proper consent, data minimization, and retention policies are not implemented.

title: Unintended Data Use
description: Child profile data could be used for purposes beyond the original intent, such as marketing, profiling, or third-party sharing without proper consent.

title: Child User Unaware of Privacy Implications
description: Child user may not fully understand the privacy implications of sharing video content, including who can see it, how long it's stored, and what metadata is collected.

title: Child Identity Revealed Through Video Content
description: Video content shared by child user may contain identifiable information about the child, their location, school, or family, potentially leading to identification and unwanted attention.

title: Video Data Intercepted in Transit
description: Video data and associated metadata (including child's identity indicators) could be intercepted during transmission between child user and video management service.

title: Video Content Tampered or Altered
description: Video management service could alter, modify, or tamper with video content after receipt, potentially changing the original message or context.

title: Child User Identified from Stored Video Data
description: Video management service could use stored video content and metadata to identify the child user, potentially linking them to other data or sharing with third parties.

title: Video Content Leaked to Unauthorized Parties
description: Video content and associated comments/likes could be leaked or accessed by unauthorized users, potentially exposing the child to inappropriate audiences.

title: Linkability of video metadata across contexts
description: Video metadata transferred between the Video Management Service and MongoDB may contain contextual information (timestamps, user IDs, session data) that could be used to link multiple video records to the same individual or session, enabling correlation of activities across different systems or time periods.

title: Identification of individuals through video metadata
description: Video metadata in transit may contain personally identifiable information (PII) such as user identifiers, timestamps, or location data that could directly identify individuals without viewing the actual video content.

title: Unauthorized access to stored video data
description: MongoDB videos collection may be accessible to unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, encryption, or authentication mechanisms, leading to exposure of stored video files and metadata.

title: Identification through stored metadata
description: Stored video metadata in MongoDB may contain PII that could be used to identify individuals, especially if metadata is not properly anonymized or if access controls are insufficient.

title: Inappropriate data sharing by Video Management Service
description: The Video Management Service may share video metadata and files with MongoDB without adequate privacy safeguards, consent mechanisms, or data minimization practices, potentially exposing more data than necessary.

title: Unauthorized access to stored child profile data
description: The MongoDB collection storing child search and watch history may not have adequate access controls, allowing unauthorized parties to access sensitive child data.

title: Excessive data retention of child browsing history
description: Child search and watch history may be retained without clear retention policies, potentially violating data minimization principles.

title: Child identification through search and watch history
description: The stored search and watch history contains data that can be used to identify specific children and their online activities.

title: Linkability of child activity data
description: Search and watch history data can be linked across sessions or devices to build comprehensive profiles of children.

title: COPPA and GDPR-K compliance concerns
description: Storing child search and watch history may violate children's privacy regulations like COPPA and GDPR-K without proper consent and safeguards.

title: Video Data Interception During Transmission
description: Video data transmitted from Parent User to Video Management Service could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transit, potentially exposing sensitive personal content.

title: Metadata Linkability
description: Metadata associated with video uploads (timestamps, file sizes, device information) could be used to link and identify the Parent User across different sessions or contexts.

title: Unauthorized Video Disclosure
description: Video Management Service may store or process uploaded videos in ways that lead to unauthorized disclosure to third parties or beyond the intended scope of processing.

title: Purpose Creep in Video Processing
description: Videos uploaded for approval/rejection may be repurposed by the Video Management Service for secondary uses not originally consented to by the Parent User.

title: Unawareness of Video Processing
description: Parent User may not fully understand how their uploaded videos will be processed, stored, or potentially shared by the Video Management Service.

title: Child Identifiable in Video Stream
description: The Video Management Service shares video content that may contain identifiable information about the child user, potentially revealing their identity, location, or activities to unauthorized parties.

title: Unauthorized Video Redistribution by Child
description: The child user may share or distribute the received video with third parties without proper authorization, leading to unauthorized disclosure of the video content.

title: Metadata Linkability in Video Stream
description: Metadata associated with the video stream (e.g., timestamps, device identifiers, IP addresses) could be used to link this video to other data about the child, creating a more comprehensive profile.

title: Excessive Data Sharing with Advertisers
description: The AI Recommendation Engine may share browsing data with third-party advertisers that exceeds what is necessary for the intended purpose, potentially exposing more user information than required.

title: User Unawareness of Data Sharing
description: Users may not be informed or aware that their browsing data is being shared with third-party advertisers, violating transparency and consent principles.

title: User Identification via Browsing Patterns
description: Browsing data transmitted in this flow may contain patterns or metadata that can be used to identify individual users or link them to specific activities.

title: Unrestricted Data Profiling by Advertisers
description: Third-party advertisers may use the received browsing data to create detailed user profiles beyond the scope of the original sharing purpose, potentially for targeted advertising or other uses.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Browsing data in transit between the AI Recommendation Engine and Third-Party Advertisers could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if proper encryption and security measures are not implemented.

title: JWT Interception During Transmission
description: JWT tokens transmitted between Authentication Service and Browser localStorage may be intercepted if not protected by HTTPS, exposing authentication credentials to network attackers.

title: JWT Accessible via XSS Attacks
description: JWT stored in browser localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript running on the page, enabling session hijacking through cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities.

title: User Identification via Stored JWT
description: JWT contains user identification information that, when stored in localStorage, can be exposed to third parties through browser inspection tools or malicious scripts.

title: Unauthorized Child Data Leakage from Process
description: The Child Profile Management process (P3) may share child history data with the parent user (EE1) without proper authentication or authorization verification, potentially leaking sensitive child information to unauthorized parties.

title: Child Identification Through Data in Transit
description: Child history data transmitted in flow DF17 contains identifying information that could be used to identify the child, even if the parent is the intended recipient. Metadata or data patterns could link the child to specific individuals.

title: Excessive Child Data Sharing
description: The process may share more child history data than necessary for the parent's review, violating data minimization principles. Full child history may be shared when only specific information is needed.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Child history data in transit through flow DF17 could be intercepted by unauthorized third parties if the transmission channel is not properly encrypted or secured.

title: Parent User Data Re-sharing
description: The parent user (EE1) may re-share or disclose the child's history information to unauthorized third parties after receiving it, extending the privacy risk beyond the intended recipient.
